claims.evidence: This is supported by the experimental methods and data presented.

claims.claim: Despite the chance to capture individual time points that display apparent initiation sites of local Ca2+ signals (firing ECC couplons), these are solely 'eager sites', whereas ECC couplons firing later disappear in the evolving global Ca2+ signal.
claims.source: Nevertheless, despite the chance to capture individual time points that display apparent initiation sites of local Ca2+ signals (i.e., firing ECC couplons; see Figure 1Aa – panel 13.7 ms), these are solely 'eager sites' (Mackenzie et al., 2001), whereas ECC couplons firing later disappear in the evolving global Ca2+ signal (see panels in Figure 1Aa later time points).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1Aa and citation to Mackenzie et al., 2001.

claims.claim: Robust de-noising with the CANDLE algorithm, which simultaneously removes Poissonian and Gaussian noise, did not significantly improve the identification of ECC couplons.
claims.source: Robust de-noising with a specialized 'CANDLE' (Coupé et al., 2012), algorithm, which simultaneously removes Poissonian and Gaussian noise, did not significantly improve this situation (Figure 1Ab).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1Ab and citation to Coupé et al., 2012.

claims.claim: The CaCLEAN method enabled identification of active ECC couplons in each of the recorded frames.
claims.source: The CaCLEAN method enabled us to identify active ECC couplons in each of the recorded frames (Figure 1B; for display reasons, we applied a slight blurring to the data; for the original CaCLEAN data, please see Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Fluorescence images rebuilt based on active ECC couplon maps resembled the original fluorescence very closely.

claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1C.

claims.claim: There is high similarity between identified release sites and the plasma membrane, with a structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.56 (average 0.57 ± 0.03, n = 46 from three animals).
claims.source: We overlaid the cumulative active couplon map (Figure 1Da) and the plasma membrane in the same confocal section (Figure 1Db) and observed high similarity between identified release sites and the plasma membrane (Figure 1Dc, the structural similarity index (SSIM) (Wang et al., 2004) was 0.56 with an average of 0.57 ± 0.03, n = 46 from three animals).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 1D and citation to Wang et al., 2004.

claims.claim: For CaCLEAN, only the upstroke period of Ca2+ transients was considered, so it was unimportant to capture the 'true' peak of the Ca2+ transient, and contraction of the cardiac myocyte did not affect the determination of the ECC couplon sites.
claims.source: Because for CaCLEAN, we only considered the upstroke period of Ca2+ transients, it was unimportant to capture the 'true' peak of the Ca2+ transient, and contraction of the cardiac myocyte did not affect the determination of the ECC couplon sites (for additional experiments concerning that important aspect, see Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm has an apparent z-resolution of approximately 1 µm under the recording conditions used.
claims.source: The peak CaCLEAN signal displayed a decreasing magnitude with an increasing distance to the plane of focus, resulting in an apparent z-resolution of approximately 1 µm under our recording conditions (see Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm is able to resolve local transients whose centres are 1 µm apart.
claims.source: From these data, we concluded that the CaCLEAN algorithm is able to resolve local transients whose centres are 1 µm apart (Figure 1—figure supplement 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claims.claim: In rat ventricular myocytes, the mean distance between RyR clusters was reported to be 1.02 µm.
claims.source: In rat ventricular myocytes, the mean distance between RyR clusters was reported to be 1.02 µm (Soeller et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature, supported by citation to Soeller et al., 2007.

claims.claim: There is good correlation between CaCLEAN-calculated maps and simulated maps of Ca2+ release sites.

claims.evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claims.claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm neither generated any false positive ECC couplons nor lost any Ca2+ release events in simulations with 1000 randomly distributed events.
claims.source: Superimposing the centres of Ca2+ release with the CaCLEANed couplon map (Figure 1—figure supplement 7E) demonstrated that the CaCLEAN algorithm neither generated any false positive ECC couplons nor lost any Ca2+ release events.
claims.evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7.

claims.claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm can reproduce the physiological 3D distribution of active ECC couplons throughout rat ventricular myocytes.
claims.source: On the basis of these tests in both the xy-plane and z-axis (Figure 1—figure supplement 4), we believe that the CaCLEAN algorithm can reproduce the physiological 3D distribution of active ECC couplons throughout rat ventricular myocytes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the validation tests shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and other supplementary figures.

claims.claim: The relationship between the CaCLEAN signal and the z-position is non-linear, resulting in an augmented functional 'rejection' of 'out of focus' Ca2+ signals and improved sectioning.
claims.source: Interestingly, the relationship between the CaCLEAN signal and the z-position was non-linear (see Figure 1—figure supplement 4), resulting in an augmented functional 'rejection' of 'out of focus' Ca2+ signals and improved sectioning, as displayed in Figure 1E.
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and Figure 1E.

claims.claim: CaCLEAN transients display a very strong preference (more than 10-fold difference in peak intensity) for 'in focus' signals over those transients alongside the ECC couplon site.
claims.source: Although the pixel Ca2+ signals were comparable at all positions (Figure 1Eb and C), the resulting CaCLEAN transients displayed a very strong preference for the 'in focus' signals over those transients alongside the ECC couplon site (more than 10-fold difference in the peak intensity).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Rebuilt fluorescence transients from the couplon map closely resembled the de-noised original data, indicating that CaCLEAN identified all active couplon sites contributing to the cellular Ca2+ transient.

claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of data shown in Figure 1Ec and e.

claims.claim: There is a very good match (correlation coefficient = 0.84 ± 0.008) between three CaCLEAN maps calculated from the same Ca2+ transient with variable noise, supporting the high reproducibility of CaCLEAN calculations.
claims.source: As depicted in Figure 2Ad and e, we found a very good match (correlation coefficient = 0.84 ± 0.008; see Figure 2Af) between the three masks, supporting the high reproducibility of CaCLEAN calculations.

claims.claim: The pattern of active ECC couplons was rather different between two consecutive Ca2+ transients (average correlation coefficient 0.47 ± 0.025) despite superimposable global Ca2+ transients.

claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: In a typical mouse atrial myocyte, 342 active ECC couplons were identified in the first transient and 352 in the second, but only 215 participated in both Ca2+ transients, indicating a re-fire rate of only 62.8%.
claims.source: We identified 342 active ECC couplons in the first transient and 352 in the second but only 215 that participated in both Ca2+ transients, indicating a re-fire rate of only 62.8%.
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the data.

claims.claim: The firing probability of ECC couplons across four consecutive Ca2+ transients demonstrated that only approximately 10% of couplons were always active.
claims.source: The firing probability of ECC couplons across four consecutive Ca2+ transients demonstrated that only approximately 10% of couplons were always active (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The reliable couplons that fire consistently were probably the eager sites described previously.

claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with previous literature, supported by citation to Mackenzie et al., 2001.

claims.claim: Rat ventricular myocytes display a well-known negative force-frequency relationship.

claims.claim: The negative force-frequency relationship in rat ventricular myocytes results, in part, from a decreased amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient with increasing stimulation frequency.

claims.evidence: This is established knowledge, supported by citations to Sipido et al., 1998 and Gattoni et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Global Ca2+ transients displayed the expected negative amplitude-frequency relationship in rat ventricular myocytes.

claims.claim: Isoproterenol substantially increased the Ca2+ transient amplitudes, particularly at low stimulation frequencies.

claims.claim: Isoproterenol promoted ECC under both low and high stimulation frequencies (intervals of 600 ms and 150 ms, respectively), albeit to a vastly different degree.

claims.claim: Isoproterenol increased the density of active ECC couplons to 803 ± 35 per 1000 μm2 at 1.7 Hz and 409 ± 185 at 6.7 Hz.

claims.source: Under both conditions, the density of recruited ECC couplons dropped monotonically, albeit with a different quantitative relationship (τctrl=107 ms vs. τiso=80 ms).

claims.claim: Isoproterenol promoted the released Ca2+ content of each active couplon at low stimulation frequencies by more than 3-fold.
claims.source: In addition to the changes in ECC couplon density, isoproterenol promoted the released Ca2+ content of each active couplon at low stimulation frequencies by more than 3-fold (Figure 3Cc).

claims.claim: The full width at half maximum (FWHM) of ECC couplons displayed small increases following isoproterenol stimulation.

claims.claim: For low, physiological stimulation frequencies, application of 10 nM isoproterenol was able to increase temporal and spatial reliability significantly.

claims.claim: At the highest pacing frequency, β-adrenergic stimulation was unable to increase reliability.

claims.claim: CaCLEAN maps closely resembled the expected distribution of ECC couplons in healthy ventricular myocytes with periodic distances of 1.7 μm, as verified by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis.
claims.source: These ECC couplon maps closely resembled the expected distribution of ECC couplons in healthy ventricular myocytes with periodic distances of 1.7 μm, as verified by a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis (Figure 3Da).

claims.claim: The FFT power of periodic distances in the couplon maps is comparable to the immunostaining results of RyRs.

claims.claim: The analysis is not strongly influenced by 'out-of-focus' Ca2+ sources that would disturb and weaken the periodicity (i.e., the power of the spatial frequency).

claims.claim: The power of the characteristic spatial frequency decreases with decreasing stimulation interval, most probably because the failure rate of ECC couplons is increasing.

claims.claim: On average, there were 0.55 couplons/µm3 in rat ventricular myocytes.

claims.claim: The value of approximately 16,500 active ECC couplons per rat ventricular myocyte correlates well with previously reported values.

claims.claim: The heart's pumping performance, measured in vivo as ejection fraction or fractional shortening, is substantially determined by the properties of the underlying cellular Ca2+ transients.

claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac physiology.

claims.claim: Cellular Ca2+ signals are the result of brief Ca2+ influxes during the cellular action potential and of the subsequent triggered Ca2+ release from the SR at sites of LTCC-RyR couplings, the so-called ECC couplons.
claims.source: These Ca2+ signals are the result of brief Ca2+ influxes during the cellular action potential and of the subsequent triggered Ca2+ release from the SR at sites of LTCC-RyR couplings, the so-called ECC couplons (Soeller et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac ECC, supported by citation to Soeller et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Strong Ca2+ buffering is thought to uncouple individual ECC couplons during electrically evoked Ca2+ transients.

claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about the effects of Ca2+ buffering, supported by citations to Cleemann et al., 1998 and Woo et al., 2002.

claims.claim: Substantial inhibition of LTCCs largely suppresses the number of firing ECC couplons.

claims.claim: The detailed properties of fundamental Ca2+ signals from ECC couplons have not been elucidated to date because of several major obstacles: the speed of the Ca2+ release process, the close proximity of numerous ECC couplons, the fast diffusion of Ca2+ ions, and the sheer amount of synchronized ECC couplons.
claims.source: Nevertheless, the detailed properties of such fundamental Ca2+ signals have not been elucidated to date because of several major obstacles: (1) the speed of the Ca2+ release process itself (in the millisecond range [Cheng et al., 1993]); (2) the close proximity of numerous ECC couplons (less than 1 μm in a typical myocyte [Hou et al., 2015]); (3) the fast diffusion of Ca2+ ions (in the range of tens of μm2/s); and (4) the sheer amount of synchronized ECC couplons (many thousands in a typical myocyte) (Bers, 2008).
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the technical challenges, supported by citations to Cheng et al., 1993; Hou et al., 2015; and Bers, 2008.

claims.claim: The CLEAN algorithm assumes that an image consists of a number of point sources for the radio signal and iteratively finds the highest value in the image and subtracts a small representation of this point source convolved with the point spread function until the radio signal has 'disappeared' below a set threshold.
claims.source: Briefly, the algorithm assumes that an image consists of a number of point sources for the radio signal. The algorithm iteratively finds the highest value in the image and subtracts a small representation of this point source convolved with the point spread function (called 'dirty beam' in radio astronomy) of the observatory until the radio signal has 'disappeared' below a set threshold (Pety, 2007).

claims.claim: The activity of individual ECC couplons in cardiac myocytes shares substantial similarity with the imaging process in radio astronomy in four key aspects: the global Ca2+ transient is the result of a large number of active ECC sites; the underlying cardiac couplon serves as the point source; the flux of Ca2+ from these ECC couplons serves as the signal-emitting process; and the Ca2+ diffusion process can be readily approximated by the convolution of a light point source with the point spread function.
claims.source: The activity of individual ECC couplons in cardiac myocytes shares substantial similarity with the imaging process in radio astronomy: (1) the global Ca2+ transient is the result of a large number of active ECC sites; (2) the underlying cardiac couplon serves as the point source; (3) the flux of Ca2+ from these ECC couplons serves as the signal-emitting process; and (4) the Ca2+ diffusion process can be readily approximated by the convolution of a light point source with the point spread function.
claims.evidence: This is an analogy drawn by the authors to justify their approach.

results.result: The CaCLEAN algorithm successfully identifies and maps active ECC couplons in intact cardiomyocytes without pharmacological intervention by combining the astronomer's CLEAN algorithm with calcium diffusion properties. The method enables identification of active ECC couplons in each recorded frame, with rebuilt fluorescence images closely resembling original data and showing high structural similarity (SSIM=0.57±0.03) between identified release sites and plasma membrane.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C44-C46 provide converging evidence that CaCLEAN successfully identifies ECC couplons, validated by the close match between rebuilt and original fluorescence (C45) and high structural similarity with plasma membrane (C46, SSIM=0.57±0.03, n=46). The method works without pharmacological intervention (C4, C47) as demonstrated across multiple experimental conditions.

results.result: CaCLEAN achieves approximately 1 μm resolution in all three optical axes (xy and z), matching the average distance between ECC couplon sites. The algorithm displays non-linear z-axis response providing >10-fold preference for in-focus signals, with optimal parameters of 60 μm²/s for Ca²⁺-dye diffusion and 30 μm²/s for ACO.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C49, C106 demonstrate 1 μm resolution through simulation studies (Figure 1—figure supplements 4-5), matching known RyR cluster spacing (C50). The non-linear z-response (C54-C55) provides strong spatial discrimination (>10-fold), and parameter optimization (C104-C105) is empirically validated in Figure 6.

results.result: CaCLEAN demonstrates high accuracy and robustness in simulations, showing good correlation with simulated Ca²⁺ release maps, no false positives or missed events in 1000-event simulations, and high reproducibility (correlation coefficient=0.84±0.008) when processing the same transient with different noise.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C52 demonstrate accuracy through simulation validation (Figure 1—figure supplements 6-7), while C57 and C103 establish robustness through noise tolerance testing (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 6). The correlation coefficient of 0.84±0.008 for identical transients with variable noise indicates strong reproducibility.

results.result: Despite indistinguishable global Ca²⁺ transients, subcellular patterns of active ECC couplons vary substantially between consecutive transients, with only 62.8% re-fire rate between two consecutive transients and only ~10% of couplons firing consistently across four transients. These consistently firing couplons likely represent previously described 'eager sites'.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C60 provide quantitative evidence of variable couplon firing patterns (correlation coefficient 0.47±0.025, n=46) despite identical global Ca²⁺ transients (Figure 2B). The low re-fire rate (62.8%) and small fraction of always-active couplons (~10%, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) are well-documented, with C61 providing reasonable interpretation linking to prior literature.

results.result: During the negative amplitude-frequency relationship in rat ventricular myocytes, ECC couplon density decreases from 653±148 to 310±146 per 1000 μm² as stimulation frequency increases from 1.7 to 6.7 Hz. Individual couplon Ca²⁺ release amplitude and size (FWHM) also decrease monotonically with frequency. Critically, firing reliability decreases substantially with increasing frequency, as evidenced by 2-4 fold increases in coefficients of variation for both spatial and temporal reliability.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C72 document quantitative changes in couplon density, amplitude, and FWHM with frequency (Figure 3C). Claims C74, C126-C130 establish decreased reliability as a key contributor to negative force-frequency relationship, supported by CV analysis (Figure 3Ce-f). The convergence of multiple independent measures (density, amplitude, FWHM, CV) provides strong support for this mechanistic conclusion.

results.result: β-adrenergic stimulation with 10 nM isoproterenol increases ECC couplon density (to 803±35 per 1000 μm² at 1.7 Hz), increases Ca²⁺ release per couplon by >3-fold at low frequencies, and significantly increases both temporal and spatial firing reliability at physiological stimulation frequencies. However, at the highest pacing frequency, β-adrenergic stimulation cannot increase reliability.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C66, C68, C70-C71 document quantitative increases in multiple parameters with isoproterenol (Figure 3C). Claims C75-C76, C131-C132 establish increased reliability at low frequencies but not at highest frequency, supported by CV analysis (Figure 3Ce-f). The frequency-dependent effect is well-documented and mechanistically consistent with known limitations of the ECC system.

results.result: 3D functional mapping reveals an average density of 0.55 couplons/μm³ in rat ventricular myocytes, corresponding to approximately 16,500 active ECC couplons per typical myocyte (volume ~30,000 μm³, n=15). This represents the first functional 3D maps of active, firing ECC couplons in living ventricular myocytes, and the value correlates well with previously reported estimates.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C84 provide quantitative 3D density measurements from experimental data (Figure 4C, n=15 cells). The calculated total of ~16,500 couplons per cell is validated by comparison with literature (C85, Bers 2008). Claims C7, C139, C147 establish the novelty of functional 3D mapping in living cells, supported by the 3D reconstruction data in Figure 4.

results.result: FFT analysis of CaCLEAN maps reveals periodic couplon distribution with characteristic distances of 1.7 μm, matching expected ECC couplon spacing in healthy ventricular myocytes. The FFT power is comparable to RyR immunostaining results. The power of characteristic spatial frequency decreases with increasing stimulation frequency, likely due to increased couplon failure rate, while the characteristic periodic distance decreases at highest frequencies, possibly due to increased diastolic Ca²⁺. Neither relationship is altered by isoproterenol.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C78 establish spatial periodicity matching known couplon spacing, validated by comparison with immunostaining (Figure 3—figure supplement 2). Claims C80-C82 describe frequency-dependent changes in FFT parameters (Figure 3Db-c), though the mechanistic interpretations (C80-C81) are speculative. The lack of isoproterenol effect on these relationships (C82) is clearly documented.

results.result: In mouse atrial myocytes, CaCLEAN successfully identifies ECC couplons that are restricted to regions near membrane invaginations, with strong structural similarity between CaCLEAN-derived couplon positions and plasma membrane. Standard denoising (CANDLE) did not significantly improve identification of ECC couplons beyond capturing 'eager sites'.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C42 establish the complex Ca²⁺ signal pattern in atrial myocytes and limitation of capturing only eager sites (Figure 1Aa, Mackenzie et al. 2001). Claim C43 documents CANDLE's insufficient improvement. Claims C98-C100, C110 demonstrate CaCLEAN's success in atrial myocytes, validated by overlay with plasma membrane (Figure 1D) and consistency with prior literature on subplasmalemmal ECC restriction.

results.result: CaCLEAN discriminates ECC couplon sites from nearby positions and functions as a deconvolution algorithm. The algorithm assumes symmetrical Ca²⁺-dye diffusion and ACO, which may be affected by barrier structures like mitochondria or SR. However, the symmetrical ACO assumption is not problematic due to highly iterative decomposition, and high temporal resolution minimizes effects of asymmetrical diffusion.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C102 establish CaCLEAN's spatial discrimination ability (Figure 1Ec, supplements 4-5) and deconvolution function. Claims C114-C119 acknowledge algorithm assumptions and limitations. The assessment that symmetrical ACO is not problematic (C117) is supported by the iterative nature (10⁻⁴ amplitude steps) and validation data, while C119 provides reasonable mitigation strategy for asymmetric diffusion effects.

results.result: Previous approaches using high Ca²⁺ buffer concentrations (1-5 mM EGTA) in patch-clamped cells have been used to study ECC couplons, but these methods might alter L-type Ca²⁺ channels and/or RyR gating. CaCLEAN results in rat ventricular myocytes are consistent with previous findings on ECC variability and extend to the negative amplitude-frequency relationship.
results.evaluation: Claims C109, C111 accurately describe previous methods from literature (Woo et al. 2002, 2005; Zahradníková et al. 2007; Janiek et al. 2012). Claim C113 provides reasonable inference about potential artifacts of high buffer concentrations. Claim C112 establishes consistency with and extension of prior work, supported by data in Figure 3Ce-f.

results.result: Functional 3D mapping demonstrates strings of coupling sites, most likely alongside T-tubular membrane structures, representing a promising step toward studying the relationship between ECC couplons and T-tubular structures in greater detail.
results.evaluation: Claim C144 is supported by 3D reconstruction data showing linear arrangements of couplons (Figure 4Bc-d). The interpretation that these represent T-tubular structures is reasonable given known cardiac myocyte architecture. Claim C145 about future applications is speculative but logically follows from the demonstrated capability.

results.result: The manuscript provides extensive background on cardiac ECC physiology, including LTCC-RyR coupling, Ca²⁺-induced Ca²⁺ release, β-adrenergic regulation, force-frequency relationships, and technical challenges in studying ECC couplons. Previous methods have been limited by requirements for pharmacological intervention or high Ca²⁺ buffering, and technical obstacles include speed of Ca²⁺ release, close proximity of couplons, fast diffusion, large numbers of synchronized events, and imaging noise.
results.evaluation: These claims (C1, C8-C39, C62-C63, C86-C96, C122, C133-C138, C143) represent established knowledge from the field, appropriately cited to primary literature (Bers 2002, 2008; Soeller et al. 2007; Wier and Balke 1999; Dorn 2010; Anderson et al. 1973; Sipido et al. 1998; Gattoni et al. 2016; Cheng et al. 1993; and others). The claims accurately describe prior work and provide appropriate context for the current study.

results.result: The study addresses gaps in knowledge about ECC couplon properties and firing reliability, with the authors suggesting that 3D functional mapping represents a milestone that will enable future studies of physiological and pathophysiological ECC changes. The approach may also be applicable to other cell types such as neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C22, C35 appropriately identify knowledge gaps that motivated the study. Claims C140-C142, C148-C149 are speculative statements about future applications and significance. While the demonstrated capabilities support potential future applications, these remain to be validated. The claims about being a 'milestone' (C140) represent author opinion rather than established fact.

results.result: Literature values for RyR cluster spacing (1.02 μm in rat ventricular myocytes) and total ECC couplon numbers (~16,500 per myocyte) are cited to validate CaCLEAN results.
results.evaluation: Claims C50 and C85 accurately cite established literature values (Soeller et al. 2007; Bers 2008) that are used for validation of the CaCLEAN method. These comparisons strengthen the validation of the new method by showing consistency with prior estimates.

results.result: Improvements in signal-to-noise ratio through use of superior Ca²⁺ sensors will help improve CaCLEAN resolution.
results.evaluation: Claim C108 is a reasonable speculation based on the demonstrated noise tolerance of the algorithm (Figure 8) and the principle that better signal quality should improve any signal processing method. However, this remains to be experimentally validated.
